education.detail.gettingStarted.welcomeD: Trazo is the first agricultural transparency platform that rewards farmers for detailed documentation. The more you document, the higher your transparency score, and the more consumers trust your products.
education.detail.gettingStarted.step1: Log all 7 types of agricultural events as they happen
education.detail.gettingStarted.step2: More documented events = higher transparency score (0-100%)
education.detail.gettingStarted.step3: Create scannable codes for each production batch
education.detail.gettingStarted.step4: Customers scan QR codes to see your transparency score
education.detail.gettingStarted.step5: Higher transparency = more consumer trust = better prices
education.detail.gettingStarted.whyTrans: 87% of consumers want to know how their food was grown, but traditional agriculture offers little visibility. Trazo bridges this gap by making your farming practices visible and trustworthy to consumers.
education.detail.gettingStarted.benefit2: Build direct relationships with conscious consumers
education.detail.gettingStarted.benefit4: Immutable proof of your farming practices
education.detail.gettingStarted.benefit5: QR codes do the storytelling for you
education.detail.gettingStarted.revoluti: Unlike carbon platforms that penalize farmers for logging events (more data = higher emissions = worse score), Trazo rewards comprehensive documentation (more events = higher transparency = better consumer trust).
education.detail.farmEvents.intro: Every agricultural activity you document increases your transparency score. Here are the 7 core event types that build consumer trust:
education.detail.farmEvents.productionDe: Core farming activities like planting, harvesting, irrigation, and equipment use
education.detail.farmEvents.productionEx: Examples: Seed planting, watering, harvesting dates, tractor operations
education.detail.farmEvents.chemicalExam: Examples: Organic fertilizer, pest control treatments
education.detail.farmEvents.soilExamples: Examples: Composting, cover crops, soil testing
education.detail.farmEvents.proTipDesc: Each event you log increases your transparency score. Aim for 90%+ transparency by documenting all major farming activities. This builds maximum consumer trust and positions you for premium pricing.
education.detail.transparencyScore.intro: Your transparency score (0-100%) is the key metric that consumers see when they scan your QR codes. It is calculated from 7 weighted categories of farming events, each with smart photo requirements that recognize not every event needs a photo.
education.detail.transparencyScore.categ: Your score is a weighted average across 7 documentation categories. Categories with higher weight have more impact on your final score.
education.detail.transparencyScore.growi: Planting, harvesting, irrigation, pruning, transplanting, cultivation
education.detail.transparencyScore.treat: Fertilizer, pesticide, fungicide, and herbicide applications
education.detail.transparencyScore.soilC: Soil tests, organic matter, composting, cover crops, pH adjustments
education.detail.transparencyScore.pestM: Scouting, beneficial releases, pest ID, trap monitoring, IPM
education.detail.transparencyScore.weath: Weather observations, farm notes, and other activities
education.detail.transparencyScore.photo: Not every event needs a photo. Trazo classifies each event type into one of three tiers based on how important visual evidence is for consumer trust.
education.detail.transparencyScore.essen: Missing photos on these events cuts their contribution in half.
All chemical applications (fertilizer, pesticide, fungicide, herbicide)
education.detail.transparencyScore.recom: Photos add value, but we understand these are harder to capture.
education.detail.transparencyScore.noPen: Photos are optional — these events score fully from documentation alone.
education.detail.transparencyScore.excel: Green trust indicators on QR page
education.detail.transparencyScore.goodI: Some photo gaps in essential events
education.detail.transparencyScore.consu: Farms with 90%+ transparency scores see 3x higher consumer engagement and 25% price premiums. Focus your photo effort on essential events (planting, harvest, chemical applications) for the biggest score improvement.
education.detail.qrCodes.progressiveLoad: Transparency score loads first (under 1.5s), then details
education.detail.qrCodes.mobileFirst: Mobile-First Design: Pages load in under 1.5s on mobile devices
education.detail.qrCodes.valueProp: Clear Value Proposition: "Scan to see how this was grown"
education.detail.qrCodes.placement: Strategic Placement: Product packaging, farmers market signs, website
education.detail.qrCodes.updates: Regular Updates: Fresh content keeps consumers engaged
education.detail.qrCodes.tracking: Track Performance: Monitor scan rates and consumer engagement
education.detail.qrCodes.instantTrust: Large transparency score with verification badges
education.detail.qrCodes.farmStory: "See exactly how this avocado was grown"
education.detail.qrCodes.successDesc: Farms using Trazo QR codes see average 78% consumer page completion rates, 340% higher engagement than traditional carbon labels, and direct consumer relationships that drive repeat purchases.
education.detail.blockchain.intro: When you finish a production, Trazo creates a permanent, tamper-proof record of everything you documented on the Polygon blockchain. Consumers can confirm this record has not been altered since submission, building trust in your documented farming practices.
education.detail.blockchain.immutable: Once recorded, farming data cannot be changed or deleted — not even by Trazo
education.detail.blockchain.global: Anyone can confirm your records have not been altered through a public blockchain explorer
education.detail.blockchain.lowCost: Polygon network enables affordable verification (about $0.01 per production)
education.detail.blockchain.trust: Replaces "trust us" with "check the immutable record yourself"
education.detail.blockchain.easy: Verification badge visible on every QR code page
education.detail.blockchain.step1: Step 1 — Document as usual: Log your farming events throughout the production cycle (planting, irrigation, fertilization, harvest, etc.)
education.detail.blockchain.step2: Step 2 — Finish your production: When you click "Finish Production," Trazo creates a digital fingerprint of ALL your documented events. This seals the record.
education.detail.blockchain.step3: Step 3 — Automatic blockchain submission: Trazo automatically submits your production's fingerprint to the Polygon blockchain in the next monthly batch.
education.detail.blockchain.step4: Step 4 — Badge appears: Your QR code page displays a "Blockchain Verified" badge with a link to the public transaction.
education.detail.blockchain.oneRecordDes: Blockchain verification covers your entire production — all events in one permanent record. You don't need to do anything special. Just document your farming as usual and finish your production when it's ready.

education.detail.carbonData.bestOfBothDe: Trazo maintains full carbon calculation accuracy for technical users while presenting consumer-friendly transparency scores that build trust and drive purchasing decisions. This dual approach serves both farmers and their diverse customer base.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.verif: All emission factors in Trazo are sourced from official EPA and USDA publications. This ensures accuracy, credibility, and alignment with government regulatory standards.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.epaGh: EPA Greenhouse Gas Emission Factors Hub
40 CFR Part 98 - The official U.S. Environmental Protection Agency source for stationary and mobile combustion emission factors. Updated annually.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.epaEg: U.S. average electricity emission factors (767.2 lbs/MWh for 2023). Accounts for the mix of energy sources in the electrical grid.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.eiaDe: U.S. Energy Information Administration - electricity generation and emissions data validation (0.81 lbs/kWh = 0.367 kg/kWh for 2023).
education.detail.carbonMethodology.ipccD: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change - N₂O emission factors for agricultural soils (EF1 = 1% of applied N, GWP = 265).
education.detail.carbonMethodology.usdaA: Farm energy use data, crop production fuel consumption, and agricultural machinery efficiency standards.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.usdaN: USDA NRCS Irrigation Pumping Plants Guide
National Engineering Handbook Chapter 8 - Energy consumption factors for irrigation pumping systems based on depth, volume, and equipment efficiency.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.pesti: Lal (2004): Herbicides 6.3±2.7, Insecticides 5.1±3.0, Fungicides 3.9±2.2 kg CO₂e/kg AI. Audsley et al.: Higher estimates (18-27 kg for herbicides).
education.detail.carbonMethodology.diese: EPA Mobile Combustion Factor: 10.21 kg CO₂ per gallon of diesel
Source: EPA Greenhouse Gas Emission Factors Hub (40 CFR Part 98) - Mobile combustion for agricultural equipment
Confidence Level: 95% - This is the most reliable emission factor as it comes directly from federal regulatory standards.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.elect: EPA eGRID U.S. Average: 0.39 kg CO₂ per kWh (delivered electricity)
Source: EPA eGRID2023 Summary Tables (767.2 lbs/MWh) + 5.12% T&D losses
Confidence Level: 95% - Based on the national electricity grid mix; actual emissions vary by region.
Irrigation pumps (deep well 200+ ft): 3.5 kWh per 1,000 gallons pumped
Irrigation pumps (standard 50-100 ft): 0.85 kWh per 1,000 gallons pumped
Wind machines (frost protection): 35 kWh per hour
Misting systems: 12 kWh per hour per acre
education.detail.carbonMethodology.ferti: Source: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 (manufacturing) + IPCC 2006/2019 Guidelines (N₂O: EF1 = 1% of applied N × 44/28 × GWP 265)
education.detail.carbonMethodology.organ: Organic fertilizers (compost, manure) have much lower emissions: only 0.5 kg CO₂/kg due to minimal manufacturing process.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.chemi: Sources: EPA Industrial Manufacturing Emission Factors, International Copper Association LCA Studies, ScienceDirect LCA Studies for organic chemicals
education.detail.carbonMethodology.calcS: When you log an event, we capture fuel used, area covered, chemicals applied, and equipment hours.
We apply the appropriate EPA/USDA emission factor based on the activity type and inputs.
All values are converted to kg CO₂e (carbon dioxide equivalent) for consistent comparison.
Total production footprint = Manufacturing emissions + Application fuel emissions
education.detail.carbonMethodology.examp: Applying 100 liters of synthetic herbicide over 5 hectares:
Manufacturing: 100L × 1.0 kg/L × 41% AI × 5.5 kg CO₂/kg = 22.55 kg CO₂e
Application fuel: 5 ha × 0.8 L diesel/ha ÷ 3.79 × 10.21 kg/gal = 10.8 kg CO₂e
education.detail.carbonMethodology.direc: Trazo calculates Direct Operational Emissions - the emissions you directly control through farming decisions. We focus on fuel combustion, fertilizer application, and equipment operation. This approach empowers you with actionable data while maintaining scientific accuracy through EPA and USDA verified emission factors.
education.detail.carbonMethodology.conti: Our emission factors are updated regularly as EPA and USDA publish new data. Last comprehensive audit: December 2025. We continuously refine our methodology based on the latest agricultural research and regulatory guidance.

education.detail.eventMastery.tip2: Include context - show the broader field/operation

education.detail.eventMastery.successDes: Successful farms document 12-15 events per production cycle with 80% photo evidence. This typically results in 90%+ transparency scores and maximum consumer trust. Remember: every documented activity tells your farm's story to consumers.
education.detail.scoreOptimization.goalD: Farms with 90%+ transparency scores command 25% price premiums and see 3x higher consumer engagement. This guide shows you exactly how to achieve these scores.
education.detail.scoreOptimization.growi: Growing Practices (30%): Planting, harvesting, irrigation, pruning — the core of your story
education.detail.scoreOptimization.treat: Treatment Details (20%): Fertilizer and chemical applications — highest consumer sensitivity
education.detail.scoreOptimization.soilD: Soil Care (18%): Soil tests, composting, cover crops — sustainability signals
education.detail.scoreOptimization.pestD: Pest Management (12%): Scouting, beneficial releases, IPM practices
education.detail.scoreOptimization.certD: Certifications (10%): Third-party trust — organic, inspections, quality standards
education.detail.scoreOptimization.weath: Weather & General (5% each): Environmental context and supplementary notes
education.detail.scoreOptimization.photo: Always photograph: planting, harvest, chemical labels
When practical: pruning, soil tests, scouting
Skip guilt-free: irrigation, weather, general notes
All other events need just 1 photo
education.detail.scoreOptimization.mista: Missing photos on essential events: Planting, harvest, and chemical application photos have the biggest impact — a 50% penalty per event
Empty high-weight categories: Having zero events in Growing Practices (30%) or Treatment Details (20%) is more costly than gaps in Weather (5%)
Batch documentation: Logging events weeks after they happened — photos must be within 7 days of the event date
Photographing everything equally: Focus your photo effort on essential events first; irrigation and weather notes don't need photos at all
Ignoring certifications: Business events now carry 10% weight — logging a single certification adds meaningful points
education.detail.scoreOptimization.bench: Target: 12-15 documented events per production cycle across all 7 categories. Photograph your essential events (planting, harvest, chemical applications) and you will consistently hit 90%+. Remember: the system rewards you for logging more, not less — every event raises your score.
